items.title: Wycliffe Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: I think they all influenced me because at one point I spent time studying their style of playing... the way Tyree plays

ctx.x: Hmmm? Not Slide. It’s not Al Grey, I can’t think of it. It’s going to come to me in a second. Oh, Tyree Glenn. I can never think of why I always get tied up with his name, Tyree. He played with Louis Armstrong. He was a great trombonist also. And I called all of those names, I think they all influenced me because at one point I spent time studying their style of playing or a particular solo that they may have done. Like the difference between the way Al Grey plays plunger, the way Tyree plays, the way that…

the way people talk from time to time. I think about the way that people laugh from time to time. So when I go to play I don’t try to play the note that fit in this chord or the scale that — I try not to make it technical but more vocal, which is what I figure that the instrument is truly for.
